subject: existing serial Relation chain; Host-declared live allocation capacity, not process heap/RSS
identity: physical allocation identity, never value, row equality, CID or reference count

included.status: assumed provider/container bound; not a measured allocation census

included.objects: each started child's Session/control/token, provider state and closures, kernel workspaces, expression roots/cursors and staged output
included.status: assumed for each actual child and every phase; independent child allocation bounds remain unproved

included.objects: completed output rows/column/occurrence arrays and value backing allocations; newly made exact edge binding/read wrappers and input arrays; next child's staged output while the predecessor remains alive
included.bound: covered by producing/consuming child bounds; uncovered edge bookkeeping must be included in parent-control
included.status: coverage premise; borrowing shares allocation IDs, independent occurrence-array copies introduce distinct IDs even with equal values

included.objects: children Ref/array and growth backing arrays; previous/current/position/pending/used/cancelled/terminal/reclaimed/cleanup_index Refs; start_next closure; advance/cancel/stopped/cleanup closures and managed execution record; edge bookkeeping not covered by a child
included.status: UNPROVED: no chain-specific sizing derivation for these objects; neither a formal-model nor a finite test discharges this bound

excluded.objects: caller-owned input payloads and preexisting sequence/registry/family/numeric configuration
excluded.reason: borrowed from existing owners; no payload copy is performed by a reference; every new wrapper or copy remains included above

excluded.objects: driver imported input and independent final output conversion outside this chain
excluded.reason: separately reserved by managed_dispatch capacity.execution_bytes; not justified by the chain theorem

excluded.objects: GC arenas, allocator fragmentation, compiler/runtime metadata, stacks, JIT/code pages and RSS
excluded.reason: process-wide physical memory is a separate unit; does not remove any chain-owned logical container allocation from the included inventory

lifetime: starting the next child retains predecessors and may create a fresh output while old output is live
some child scratch may release early; the full declared bound remains a conservative reservation
false/error cleanup retains that child's obligation and every still-owned allocation
terminal observation alone does not authorize releasing the reservation
reverse cleanup releases readers before producers; shared allocation remains live until its last owner is done

parentAllowance.rationaleFound: live child sessions, provisional outputs, and handles; same coefficient as general node/container allowances
parentAllowance.missing: enumerated parent allocation sizes, array growth and retained capacity, target-specific representation and an upper-bound derivation
parentAllowance.disposition: explicit undischarged premise; no unconditional live-byte guarantee; a product sizing/reservation change requires separate evidence and PR
